items.quote: Reports must be submitted to the Investigations Office, where they will be addressed in accordance with the Procedures to this Policy, which include an initial review as set out under section 4 of the Procedures to determine whether the allegations contained in the Report fall within UBC’s Jurisdiction to Investigate.
items.reason: The policy is a dedicated sexual misconduct policy with its own reporting and investigation process managed by the Investigations Office.
The policy does not contain an explicit commitment to make the policy text itself publicly available.

items.quote: Reports must be submitted to the Investigations Office, where they will be addressed in accordance with the Procedures to this Policy, which include an initial review as set out under section 4 of the Procedures to determine whether the allegations contained in the Report fall within UBC’s Jurisdiction to Investigate.
items.reason: The policy states that reports must be submitted to the Investigations Office in writing, but does not provide specific contact details or step-by-step instructions on how to do so.

items.quote: An individual’s sexual reputation or history of sexual activity cannot be submitted as evidence to prove that it was likely that the individual provided Consent.
items.reason: The policy explicitly prohibits submitting an individual's sexual reputation or history of sexual activity as evidence of consent.

items.quote: Investigations are fact-finding processes. They are not adversarial processes and hearings will not be held as part of the investigatory process.
items.reason: The policy guarantees that hearings will not be held, ensuring there is no face-to-face confrontation or direct cross-examination during the investigation.

items.quote: However, this section does not prevent: 8.2.1 any participants in the Investigation from disclosing information about themselves, or information that they have obtained outside the Investigation;
items.reason: The policy explicitly states that confidentiality requirements do not prevent participants from disclosing information about themselves or information obtained outside the investigation.

items.quote: UBC is committed to respecting the rights of those who Disclose to make their own decisions about accessing support services and assistance, making a Report, or pursuing external processes such as criminal or civil actions (whether instead of or in addition to pursuing UBC’s processes).
items.reason: The policy explicitly respects the survivor's right to choose between institutional processes, external processes (like criminal or civil actions), both, or neither.

items.quote: An individual who makes a Disclosure or Report will not be subject to actions for violating any applicable UBC policy, rules, or regulations related to alcohol or drug use at the time the alleged Sexual Misconduct occurred.
items.reason: The policy provides explicit amnesty from disciplinary action for drug or alcohol use at the time of the incident.

items.quote: The Director of Investigations will set the timelines for each Investigation and may adjust the timelines in an Investigation at any time.
items.reason: The timelines are adjustable at any time at the discretion of the Director of Investigations, making them non-binding.

items.quote: Assistance will be available to Members of the UBC Community who have Disclosed or Reported and may include: student residence re-location or short-term emergency student housing; class schedule changes; provision of academic concessions; emergency funding for students; safety planning; temporary work reassignment, location reassignment, or scheduling changes; and the implementation of safety measures which may include temporary interim restrictions pursuant to the At-Risk Behaviour Policy (SC13).
items.reason: The policy states that assistance will be available and 'may include' interim measures like residence relocation, class schedule changes, and work reassignment, making these specific measures discretionary.

items.quote: student, defined as any person, including co-op and exchange students, registered or enrolled in any component of a for-credit academic or training program or course at UBC, or any class of learners designated by resolution of the Senate as students;
items.reason: The policy's scope explicitly includes co-op students within the definition of 'Members of the UBC Community'.

items.quote: The Director of Investigations will inform the Complainant of any disciplinary outcomes that the University Counsel has authorized the Director to disclose in accordance with section 7.5 of these Procedures.
items.reason: Informing the complainant of disciplinary outcomes is limited and subject to authorization by the University Counsel.

items.quote: Annually, UBC will publicly report, in the aggregate and without identifying personal information, the number of: requests for services received by the Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Offices; and Reports received by the Investigations Office;
items.reason: The policy commits to publicly reporting annual aggregate numbers of requests, reports, investigations, and resolutions.

items.quote: UBC is committed to reviewing this Policy at least once every three years, in consultation with students and such other Members of the UBC Community as UBC deems appropriate in accordance with the Regulatory Framework Policy (GA2).
items.reason: The policy requires a review at least once every three years, which is longer than the two-year benchmark.
